 European delegates will join the next round of peace talks with Ukraine and Russia, US envoy Jared Kushner says, after a brisk day of diplomacy saw him and Steve Witkoff meet both Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russia’s Vladimir Putin.
 After speaking to Putin in Moscow earlier, Kushner said: “Both sides have now agreed to expand the next round of negotiations to include our European partners.”
 “This will allow us to address the broader postwar European security agreements alongside the territorial issues between Ukraine and Russia,” Kushner, US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law who acts as one of the country’s top diplomats despite holding no official role within the administration, posted on X on Thursday.
 The sweeping declaration came after Russian, Ukrainian and US negotiators engaged in the first talks to end the war for months – with no clear breakthrough.
 As of Friday, European leaders have not yet publicly assigned a representative for any further discussions.
 The Kremlin offered no firm response to the possibility of European involvement and doubled down on key territorial demands.
 Meanwhile, Kyiv’s forces on the ground were unable to fend off concurrent Russian salvos. That followed repeated disruptions to Starshield – a military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink service critical to Ukraine’s military operations.
 Zelensky told reporters in Dublin the recent discussions gave Kyiv “hope that we will end this war.”
 Speaking alongside Witkoff and Kushner on Thursday night, Zelensky also said that a recently agreed prisoner of war exchange would be the biggest since the start of the war, calling the swap “a real result.”
 Reuters 
 Just before the US envoys departed Moscow, Witkoff told CNN’s Frederik Pleitgen at Vnukovo Airport: “I think progress was made. I think it was made earlier today. People didn’t think that we were going to restart trilateral. We’ve restarted it. We’ve set a new meeting.”
 “This is what President (Donald) Trump wants to see,” he added.
 Putin claimed that Moscow had “never been opposed to engaging in dialogue with Europe.” “We have never broken it off,” he said in the meeting with both White House envoys.
 “We are aware that territorial issues are viewed differently by the two sides,” Putin said. “This, as I have already said, will always be a bone of contention,” he added.
 While Ukraine has long argued that Europe should be at the main negotiating table, Moscow has previously resisted such efforts.
 US envoys Steve Witkoff (left) and Jared Kushner (center) meet Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky (right) at the Airport in Dublin, Ireland, on Thursday. 
 Peter Morrison/AP 
 European security plans ‘important step’
 On Friday, the Kremlin said it remained open to engaging with Europe, suggesting the next round of negotiations could happen “in the foreseeable future.”
 “Putin has never refused to engage with the Europeans,” the Kremlin’s spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, told journalists on Friday. “If the Europeans truly have someone who is authorized to hold discussions… then, of course, we would be prepared to talk with them.”
 Peskov stopped short of endorsing a European representative.
 Earlier this week, Putin’s foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov – while confirming that trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the US would continue – appeared to play down the suggestion that European representatives would join them, hinting “they need to decide whether they want peace or a continuation of the war.”

 Asked if Russia was suspicious of Europe’s intentions, Russian presidential special envoy Kirill Dmitriev told CNN Thursday: “I think working on European security is definitely a great, important step for Europe. And frankly, people who care about Europeans and their lives, of course, want European security to be strong.”
 Russia's President Vladimir Putin (right) accompanied by Kremlin officials at a meeting with Kushner and Witkoff, in Moscow on Thursday. 
 Vyacheslav Prokofyev/AFP/Getty Images 
 Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov also criticized the presence of European officials in the UAE city earlier this week, saying their involvement was not a “promising approach.”
 Meanwhile, Ushakov said Putin and Trump will “continue discussions” about Ukraine during a planned bilateral meeting at the APEC summit in China.
 Before the meeting with the US envoys, Zelensky joined other world leaders in Dublin earlier on Thursday for the European Political Community summit, where the discussions in Abu Dhabi were discussed, as well as additional sanctions on Russia.
 Kyiv faces drone attack
 Rescuers and Red Cross volunteers carry the body of a woman killed by a Russian drone strike in Kyiv on Thursday. 
 Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters 
 Despite the flurry of diplomacy, the latest push for peace has not afforded Ukraine respite from the daily barrage of Russian attacks.
 At least 10 people were killed and 48 others injured in the country from Thursday into Friday, according to regional officials.

 Pentagon watchdog declines bipartisan request to investigate Starshield slowdowns in Ukraine 
 3 min read 
 CNN has reached out to the White House and the Pentagon. SpaceX, the company which owns Starshield, told CNN that there had been no change in its service.
 In October too, Ukraine said speed limits were imposed on Starshield satellite terminals, as the relationship between Kyiv and Washington deteriorated. Trump denied approving that decision, while Musk said the Trump administration was behind the restrictions.
 This story has been updated with additional developments. 
 CNN’s Svitlana Vlasova, Katharina Krebs and Anna Chernova contributed reporting.
